stem: Draw the graph of the linear function $f(x) = {=linear(m, b)}$. Drag two points so that the line is its graph.
solution: Write the rule as $y = f(x)$ and find two ordered pairs.
Put $x = 0$: $y = b$, so the graph cuts the y-axis at $(0, b)$. This point is not the origin when the rule has a constant term.
Put $x = 1$: $y = m + b$, a second ordered pair.
Plot the two pairs and draw the straight line through them.
notes: The anchor list for lo:pp3u1-4-3 is empty, so parent_question_id is left blank. Samuel should assign the book's graphing exercise. Only intercept-wrong is mapped: the correct slope with the line forced through (0, 0) is the signature of the origin misconception. A student who has the right slope but the wrong intercept for another reason would also fire it. slope-sign-flipped, slope-inverted, vertical-line and off-target are left unmapped because this objective has no misconception that names them. The instances are all inside the instrument limits: whole-number m, |m| ≤ 5, b in −5..5. A constant-function instance (m = 0) could be added as a later row.
